HeroName: Ioánnis Raoúl Petralífas, Protovestiarios of Nicaea
Description: Ioánnis Raoúl Petralífas, holding the exalted rank of Protovestiarios, was one of the most powerful military magnates and chivalric commanders of the Nicaean Empire. Combining Norman martial lineage from the Petraliphas family with ancient Byzantine nobility from the House of Raoul, John was famed for immense physical strength, tactical audacity, and frontline valor across Thrace and Anatolia. His union with Emperor Michael VIII's brilliant niece, Theodora Raoulaina, placed him at the heart of imperial statecraft. At the Battle of Pelagonia in 1259, John spearheaded devastating cataphract counter-charges that tore through the ranks of Frankish knights. An unbending traditionalist, he valued Orthodox dogmatic purity above courtly favor. When Michael VIII persecuted anti-unionist monks following the Council of Lyons, John openly championed the dissident cause, confronting the emperor to protect Orthodox autonomy. Revered for chivalric honor, integrity, and soldierly camaraderie, John Raoul embodied the martial backbone of the restored empire. Across the mud of Pelagonia, John Raoul led iron wedges through three successive Frankish lines, unhorsing dozens of Latin barons in single combat. An idol of the legions, he led every charge personally, treating wounded troopers with tender care while executing cowards without mercy. When Michael VIII demanded oaths to the Union of Lyons, John renounced all courtly honors on the palace floor, throwing down his staff of office to defend Orthodox traditionalists, his name honored across Byzantium.
SpeechStyle: His voice booms with battlefield authority and unbending moral honor, completely fearless before imperial wrath or hostile knights.
